# CTS — OCV reconfiguration in units of the 2015-2017 reference, month by month

*generated by `code/cts/fig_cts_ocv_reconfiguration_cts.py`; the metric is the pre-registered one of `code/sds/ocv_reconfigure_spec.md` (behaviour block, log transform, reference MAD), read here as a monthly series. It is not a new test, and it carries none.*

Champlain Towers South, Surfside (FL): one support-sized chip per acquisition (39 x 145 cells, 225 support cells, 30 m guard, 200 m ring), 178 acquisitions in the ASC orbit. The record splits into a **reference** of 35 chips (2015-09-21 … 2017-12-15), the **series** of 101 chips on 42 months (2018-01 … 2021-06), and 42 post-collapse chips that are counted and never plotted.

```
z(month) = ( median(log x_month) - median(log x_ref) ) / MAD(log x_ref)
x        = gamma2, P            both on the log scale
R        = rms over the two dimensions (gamma2, P)
ref      = 2015-09-21 .. 2017-12-15   n = 35 chips on 20 months
series   = 2018-01-08 .. 2021-06-21   101 chips on 42 months, 1-3 per month
```

The reference is drawn from the years *before* the series, so the origin of everything below is the site's own long-run state and not a baseline chosen after the fact. `0` on both axes is that state; it is not a norm and not a threshold.

## The reference is the origin

| dim | column | transform | n_ref | median (log) | median | MAD (log) | 1 MAD = | pooled MAD (log) | scale used |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| gamma2 | `gamma2_mask` | log | 35 | -4.7678 | 0.008499 | 1.1629 | x3.199 | 0.8651 | `mad` |
| P | `P` | log | 35 | -1.4343 | 0.2383 | 0.2401 | x1.271 | 0.1899 | `mad` |

Both dimensions keep the reference MAD: n_ref = 35 is above the `SCALE_MIN_REF = 10` of the 2026-10-22 amendment, so the pooled MAD is **not** substituted. It travels beside the reference as the declared sensitivity — `z_pooled` in the JSON reads the same r from the pooled median and the pooled MAD of the whole record, an affine image of z rather than a second estimate, quantified under *What the series shows*. One MAD of gamma2 is a factor x3.199 on that dimension and x1.271 on P.

The reference is *pooled*, not a run of adjacent images: 35 chips over 20 months, with 8 months empty (2015-11, 2015-12, 2016-01, 2016-02, 2016-03, 2016-05, 2016-06, 2016-08) — the acquisition gaps of the 2015-2017 record (`data/cts/cts_acquisition_census.md`). That is the population the origin stands for, and the moving-block draw resamples it in date order so a draw keeps neighbouring chips together.

`n` is the number of chips the month's median rests on, `✱` marks a month at or below `SMALL_N = 6` — here **every** month, 42 of 42 — and `–` is a cell the record does not contain, never a zero. The interval is the *reference's* uncertainty: 2000 circular moving-block draws of the 35 reference chips with the reference median **and** scale re-estimated inside each draw, the month's chips held fixed. It answers "how well is the origin known", not "how well is the month known".

## What the series shows

**The last month before the collapse sits on the reference.** 2021-06 carries 2 chips (2021-06-09, 2021-06-21): z(gamma2) = +0.39 with a 95 % reference-uncertainty interval of [-0.17, +1.20], z(P) = -0.23 [-1.69, +0.41], and R = 0.32 against a reference band of 0.27–2.47. Both intervals cover zero, and R is inside the band, so the terminal month reads as *the reference*, not as a departure from it.

**The largest excursions are earlier, in 2019-2020.** gamma2 reaches -2.29 in 2020-01 (n = 2) and +1.11 in 2019-01 (n = 3); P reaches -0.86 in 2019-10 (n = 3) and +1.85 in 2019-08 (n = 3). Beyond ±2 MAD lie 1 gamma2 month(s) (2020-01) and no P month.

**No 2021 month is an outlier.** The largest |z| in any 2021 month is 1.47, well inside the ±2 MAD band: the last 6 months run inside the band on both axes, so the record does not end on an excursion.

**The block magnitude stays bounded.** R peaks at 1.91 in 2020-01 (n = 2), and the reference's own 95th percentile is 2.47: no month reaches it. R is an RMS over two dimensions, so one coordinate can carry it — which is why panel (c), not R alone, is the reading.

**The series oscillates; it does not drift.** gamma2 is negative in 23 of 42 months, P in 7 of 42, and the longest unbroken run of one sign is 5 months for gamma2 and 15 for P: a stretch, not a trend. A drift toward the collapse would have to be monotone, and this is not.

**The pooled sensitivity is the same picture from another origin.** `z_pooled` re-centres the same r on the pooled median of all 178 chips and re-scales by the pooled MAD, so it is an affine image of z: 1.344·z +0.033 for gamma2 and 1.264·z -0.577 for P. 9 month(s) change side under it, all within 0.41 MAD of zero; no excursion moves, and it is declared as a sensitivity, not as a second estimate.

**One sentence.** Between 2018-01 and 2021-06 the site oscillates around its own 2015-2017 state with the widest deviations in 2019-2020, and the last month that exists is not one of them.

## What it does not say

* **The binding limit is sampling, not SNR.** A month rests on 1-3 chips, so every month is `thin` (`n < SMALL_N = 6`) and a one-chip month's "median" *is* that single chip. The monthly marker is the median of the chips that exist, not of the month; a month with no acquisition would be a gap, not a value.
* **The interval belongs to the reference.** It says how well a 35-chip origin is known under a resampling of those chips. It is not a confidence interval for a monthly value: the month's own sampling noise is not in it, and for a one-chip month that noise is the whole spread of the record.
* **The series stops at the collapse, deliberately.** The 42 acquisitions after 2021-06-24 (2021-07-03 … 2022-12-25) are bare sand, not the building, and their intensity is moisture-driven; they are counted in the audit and carry no value here. Including them, or the demolition of 2021-07-05, would compare two different measured objects.
* **No precursor claim.** The metric is descriptive: it says where the last available month (2021-06) sits, and that month is on the reference. Nothing between that month and the collapse was measured by this record — the next acquisition is after the event — so a series of 1-3 chips per month cannot time, detect or exclude a precursor, and no test is run that would pretend otherwise.
* **No test, no dose, no partner.** The sds H1/H2 machinery needs at least two states per block and, for a dose, an ordered ladder; here one state is sampled monthly. So there is no p-value, no Holm family and no cosine, and these magnitudes are in the reference's own units — they are not comparable to Haltern's, KDLO's or Morandi's.

## Reproduce

```
python3 code/cts/fig_cts_ocv_reconfiguration_cts.py            # data + figure
python3 code/cts/fig_cts_ocv_reconfiguration_cts.py --selftest
python3 code/cts/fig_cts_ocv_reconfiguration_cts.py --verify
bash figures/cts/fig_cts_ocv_reconfiguration_cts.sh
```

The run reads `data/cts/support/cts_ocv_channels.csv` (sha256 `3965a15b2053dc0b…`) and `data/cts/support/cts_ocv_channels_meta.json`, and writes `data/cts/ocv_reconfiguration_cts.json`, `data/cts/ocv_reconfiguration_cts_table.csv`, `figures/cts/fig_cts_ocv_reconfiguration_cts.jpg` and this file. No timestamp enters either output, so a second run is byte-identical.

## The figure

* **(a)** z(gamma2) by month: one dot per chip (light), the month's median (filled), the reference's +-2 MAD band (grey), the 95 % reference-uncertainty bar, the chip count `n` in the strip at the bottom, and the collapse of 2021-06-24 as the red cut. A month with `n = 1` is drawn open, because its "median" is a single chip.
* **(b)** z(P) on the same axis and the same reference — the two panels are read together, never as two independent verdicts.
* **(c)** the plane: the origin is the reference state, the grey cloud is the 35 reference chips, the path runs 2018-01 -> 2021-06 and is coloured by year, the thin arrows are the per-year medians, and the last pre-collapse month is ringed.
* **(d)** R = rms(z gamma2, z P) per month against the empirical 5-95 % band of the reference chips' own R.
